[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?

[00:30] Priya: main objective for us is predictability — we need predictable latency under load and better unit economics than our current in-house ops. We're open to committed capacity if the math works.
[00:42] Laura: and we need eu-west for GDPR data residency plus lower latency for our EU customers.
[00:50] Samir: understood; on residency we support region pinning and we can enable eu-west as an additional region on Dedicated, note pricing differs slightly because of capacity commitments.
[01:05] Marcus: couple of constraints — our infra team requires SAML SSO + SCIM, KMS for envelope encryption, and audit logs forwarded to our Splunk. Also we need network diagrams for procurement.
[01:20] Jenna: we have SAML and SCIM in the private control plane and Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS (we've integrated with AWS KMS and HSM options). On logs we can set up log forwarding — I'll put the runbook link in the notes.
[01:35] Laura: do you have SOC2 and ISO certs? Our security team will ask.
[01:40] Samir: yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 — I'll share the certs and the security pack with the network diagram after this call.
[01:50] Priya: timeline — we're targeting contract signed by mid-April so we can provision buffer capacity by May. Is that feasible?
[02:00] Samir: yes, mid-April is feasible if we lock committed capacity numbers and get procurement docs started; pricing sheet and terms will be shared.

[06:12] Jenna: ok diving into the perf/benchmark part — for your current workload distribution Laura mentioned mostly short chats (~40 tokens avg) with bursts during promotions up to 8k concurrent requests across regions. For capacity planning we recommended a baseline dedicated pool equivalent to 12 A100-sim nodes with burst headroom to 20, which based on our qps model meets your 99th percentile latency SLO of sub-400ms for the short prompts.
[06:35] Marcus: 12 nodes sounds high; can you show the math? our finance team will poke holes in that number.
[06:42] Jenna: sure — high level: model choice is a 16B variant, tokenization and KV cache hit rate assumptions — if your KV cache hit rate is 60% steady-state we see ~35% lower GPU work. We'll share the spreadsheet; it's a bit approximate until we run your real sample prompts.
[07:05] Laura: when you say KV cache, is that prefix caching of repeated prompts? How does that behave with many tenants?
[07:12] Jenna: yes prefix/KV cache — for multi-tenant config we can enable per-customer cache or global cache with TTLs; tradeoffs are memory usage vs hit rate. We'll show options in the benchmark.
[07:28] Marcus: what about quantization — are you recommending int8 for inference? Licenses?
[07:33] Jenna: we support quantized execution; recommended profiles depend on perf vs quality. For the 16B we often run a mixed q4/q8 config; quality regressions are small for scoring tasks but you should validate on your prompts. We'll include model + quantization recommendations.

[10:10] Laura: pricing — our CFO will want committed monthly cost and a comparison to on-demand hosted and our current cloud VMs. Can you provide a delta analysis?
[10:18] Samir: absolutely — I'll put together a committed capacity pricing sheet with committed discounts and show the per-token amortized cost vs on-demand. Also include a short TCO comparing doing it in-house.
[10:30] Priya: procurement will need contract language around data residency, support SLOs and liability caps — any standard enterprise terms?
[10:36] Samir: yes we have enterprise terms for Dedicated — SLA options and liability language, we can provide a draft and engage legal.

[15:00] Marcus: from a tech perspective, we want a 2-hour benchmark first in a staging slice with production-like traffic, and if the numbers look good we'll rotate traffic gradually. How long to provision a dedicated pool after contract?
[15:10] Samir: typical lead time is 2-3 weeks to provision the physical pool depending on region and capacity; eu-west provisioning may add a week depending on availability. If you want faster we can do an interim hosted to validate and then cutover.
[15:28] Marcus: can we do a hybrid? keep some traffic on hosted while dedicated ramps up?
[15:32] Jenna: yes smart routing can split traffic by policy (region, customer tier) — we can route EU traffic to eu-west Dedicated once ready and keep other traffic on hosted.

[18:40] Laura: ok risks — we're worried about cold-start latency and the p99 tail under burst. What mitigation do you offer?
[18:47] Jenna: we have warm pools and continuous batching, plus KV prefix caching. For tails we recommend autoscale buffer and pre-warming during big campaigns. We'll run burst tests to see tail behavior.
[19:05] Priya: what about failover? if eu-west has an outage can we fall back to us-east without violating residency?
[19:12] Samir: fallbacks are policy driven — for regulated flows you can disable cross-region failover, but for lower-priority endpoints you can allow cross-region fallback. We'll document options.

[22:00] Marcus: security deep dive — on KMS integration, do you support external HSM and customer-managed keys?
[22:08] Jenna: yes customer-managed KMS is supported; integration with BYOK and HSM is available for Private/Dedicated. We'll include the KMS architecture diagram.
[22:20] Laura: audit logs — can we get token-level cost/latency traces and export them?
[22:26] Samir: yes Console exposes token-level cost, latency breakdowns and tracing hooks; logs can be exported to your SIEM.

[25:00] Priya: renewal terms — we're approaching renewal in late April — we're evaluating a 12-month committed term with quarterly reviews and an option to increase capacity in Q4. Any flexibility on term length?
[25:12] Samir: we commonly do 12 or 24 month terms; for larger commitments we can negotiate stepped pricing and renewal credits. I can draft options for 12 vs 24 months and show the price delta.
[25:30] Priya: great. Also want to ensure we have a pilot clause — if perf regressions happen we'll have escape hatches.
[25:38] Samir: we can include guardrail language and a limited pilot period where you can validate KPIs before committing fully.

[30:15] Jenna: benchmark logistics — Marcus, we'll need a stable traffic replay or synthetic harness plus the sample prompts. Ideal window is 2 hours, we'll do steady-state, then 15m burst ramp, then 15m cooldown, and collect p50/p95/p99 and cost per token metrics.
[30:30] Marcus: I can whip up a replay from our logging cluster; will share credentials for a staging slice.
[30:36] Jenna: perfect. Also note we'll measure KV cache hit rate — please include any caching rules or prompt templating.

[33:45] Laura: procurement question — do you have an approved data processing addendum for EU customers?
[33:50] Samir: yes we have a DPA and standard DP clauses, I'll send the executed template with the SOC2 attachments.

[36:00] Samir: ok circling back — quick recap: Samir to send pricing and security pack today, Jenna to coordinate benchmarks and testing windows, Laura to share prompts and histograms, Marcus to provision staging slice and share access, Priya to push procurement timeline (mid-April target).
[36:18] Priya: one more thing — support model during ramp, any notes on SRE involvement?
[36:24] Jenna: we offer a 24/7 support add-on for Dedicated plus an assigned technical account manager for enterprise accounts. We'll include that in the proposal.

[40:00] Laura: are there any known vendor lock-in concerns? we currently worry about model portability and being stuck on a provider.
[40:08] Samir: we try to be model-agnostic and support standard export/import formats; also provide guidance for fallback to hosted or self-hosted variants. We'll include migration playbooks.

[43:12] Marcus: on cost — will your committed capacity pricing include a commitment to fixed throughput (e.g., tokens/hour) or is it an RT capacity modeled as node-hours?
[43:20] Samir: typically it's a reserved node pool (node-hours) with a promised baseline throughput; we can show the mapping to expected tokens/hour and provide overage/burst pricing.
